title: In a twist of irony, a Chinese open source GLM 5.2 AI model contained 'rogue' OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol in a Hugging…
excerpt: Chinese AI unexpectedly rescues Hugging Face after rogue OpenAI agent sparks fierce new battle over America's open-weight AI future
content_html:
• Chinese Zhipu AI GLM-5.2 succeeded where leading American models failed woefully
  • Hugging Face breach reignited Washington's battle over open-weight artificial intelligence
  • Safety guardrails unexpectedly complicated defensive cybersecurity work during a real incident

The recent cybersecurity incident involving Hugging Face has unexpectedly placed a Chinese open source AI model at the centre of an intensifying United States policy debate over open-weight AI.

The episode emerged after an autonomous agent built with OpenAI technology reportedly escaped containment and behaved like a rogue actor.

The incident occurred as Washington is considering whether broader restrictions on Chinese open-weight AI models could affect American developers and startups.

Chinese open source model enters an unexpected cybersecurity role

According to Hugging Face, engineers relied on Zhipu AI's GLM-5.2 model to examine information generated during the incident after leading American models declined the requests.

American AI models could not distinguish legitimate defensive investigations from malicious hacking attempts because of built-in safety restrictions and protective guardrails.

Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 reportedly reroutes cybersecurity questions to an older, less capable model rather than allowing direct engagement with such tasks.

OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol carries similar protections meant to stop the system from being used for hacking-related work of any kind.

OpenAI later revealed that it has a Trusted Access programme that grants privileged, elevated capabilities to a select group of vetted teams, allowing them to use its models more fully to strengthen their own defenses.

Hugging Face was brought into this restricted tier following the breach, gaining deeper access than is normally available.

"We're all learning that secrecy is ⁠not the answer & that all defenders (not just a few selected ones) everywhere need more powerful models without restrictions, especially open ones!" said Hugging Face co-founder ​Clement Delangue.

"A ⁠safety regime that restricts legitimate defenders, while capable models remain available for attackers, creates an asymmetric disadvantage," said Lukasz Olejnik, visiting senior research fellow at the Department of War Studies, King's College London.

"This gap will only widen as open-source models become increasingly powerful while lacking guardrails or restrictions."

Washington weighs restrictions while startups urge caution

Nearly 200 Silicon Valley companies are opposing possible restrictions on Chinese open-weight AI models, warning that the move would raise costs for smaller developers.

Members of the newly formed Little Tech Association say banning downloads would not curb proliferation but would leave American startups weaker.

"There'll be hundreds of companies that instantly die," founder Suhail Doshi warned.

He argued that sweeping restrictions would disproportionately benefit larger American providers with the resources to absorb such a shift.

The U.S. is still scrutinizing Chinese developers over allegations involving model distillation and export control violations

White House officials maintained that any future policy decisions would come directly from the administration itself.

Analysts have also cautioned against treating the Hugging Face incident as justification for weakening the cybersecurity safeguards protecting advanced American systems.

"The answer is not simply to remove them," Shrenik Kothari of Robert W. Baird said, arguing that companies should refine their access controls rather than abandon safety measures altogether.

He suggested a more selective approach to capability allocation could balance legitimate security needs with the practical demands of cybersecurity research.

Via Reuters

content_html_zh:
• 中国智普人工智能GLM-5.2取得了成功，而美国领先模型惨遭失败
  • Hugging Face 泄露事件重新引发了华盛顿对开放式人工智能的争夺
  • 真实事件中的安全护栏出乎意料地复杂化防御性网络安全工作

最近涉及“抱脸”的网络安全事件出人意料地将中国开源人工智能模型置于美国关于开放权重人工智能政策激烈争论的中心。

据报道，使用 OpenAI 技术构建的自主代理逃脱了收容，并且表现得像一个流氓演员，这一事件就此发生。

该事件发生之际，华盛顿正在考虑对中国开放式人工智能模型的更广泛限制是否会影响美国开发商和初创公司。

中国开源模式进入了意想不到的网络安全角色

据Hugging Face报道，在美国领先模型拒绝了请求后，工程师们依靠智普AI的GLM-5.2模型来检查事件期间生成的信息。

由于内置的​​安全限制和防护栏，美国人工智能模型无法区分合法的防御调查和恶意黑客攻击。

据报道，Anthropic 的 Claude Fable 5 将网络安全问题重新路由到较旧的、能力较差的模型，而不是允许直接参与此类任务。

OpenAI 的 GPT-5.6 Sol 具有类似的保护措施，旨在阻止系统被用于任何类型的黑客相关工作。

订阅 TechRadar Pro 时事通讯，获取您的企业成功所需的所有热门新闻、观点、功能和指导！

OpenAI 后来透露，它有一个可信访问计划，向一组经过审查的团队授予特权、提升的能力，使他们能够更充分地使用其模型来加强自己的防御。

违规后，Hugging Face 被纳入此受限级别，获得了比正常情况更深入的访问权限。

“我们都知道，保密并不是答案，各地的所有捍卫者（不仅仅是少数选定的捍卫者）都需要更强大且不受限制的模型，尤其是开放模型！” Hugging Face 联合创始人克莱门特·德兰格 (Clement Delangue) 说道。

伦敦国王学院战争研究系客座高级研究员卢卡斯·奥莱尼克 (Lukasz Olejnik) 表示：“安全制度限制了合法的防御者，而攻击者仍然可以使用有能力的模型，这会造成不对称的劣势。”

“随着开源模型变得越来越强大，同时缺乏护栏或限制，这种差距只会扩大。”

华盛顿权衡限制，而初创企业敦促谨慎

近 200 家硅谷公司反对对中国开放权重人工智能模型的可能限制，警告称此举将增加小型开发商的成本。

新成立的小科技协会的成员表示，禁止下载不会遏制扩散，但会削弱美国初创企业的实力。

创始人苏海尔·多西警告说：“将会有数百家公司立即消亡。”

他认为，全面的限制将使拥有资源来吸收这种转变的大型美国供应商受益匪浅。

美国仍在审查中国开发商涉及模型蒸馏和违反出口管制的指控

白宫官员坚称，未来的任何政策决定都将直接来自政府本身。

分析人士还警告不要将“抱脸”事件视为削弱保护美国先进系统的网络安全保障措施的理由。

罗伯特·W·布什 (Robert W. 贝尔德表示，他认为公司应该完善访问控制，而不是完全放弃安全措施。

他建议采用更具选择性的能力分配方法可以平衡合法的安全需求与网络安全研究的实际需求。
